title: Report every step of a partially applied VCF Operations notification change
prompt: Implement the exported New-VcfOpsOutboundNotification function in src/VcfOps.OutboundNotification/VcfOps.OutboundNotification.psm1. The module onboards an outbound notification on VCF Operations 9.0 through the prerequisite VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops PowerCLI module, and it receives an already connected VCF Operations Server object that must be passed to every SDK call. Apply the change in three ordered steps: create the notification plugin instance with Invoke-VcfOpsCreateAlertPlugin and no enabled flag, activate that instance with Invoke-VcfOpsUpdateAlertPlugin by resending it with the returned pluginId and enabled set to true, then bind the notification rule with Invoke-VcfOpsCreateNotificationPluginRule. The third step fails when the server has no matching notification template. When that happens the first two steps have already changed the appliance: report them as Succeeded, do not roll the change back, and do not report the run as if nothing had been applied. Return one object with Succeeded, PluginId, RuleId, RequiresCleanup and a Steps collection of exactly three entries in order, each carrying Index, OperationId, Status (Succeeded, Failed or Skipped), StatusCode and Message. PluginId and RuleId are the identifiers assigned by the server, or an empty string when the corresponding resource was not created. RequiresCleanup is true when the run failed after at least one step applied. For a failed step, StatusCode is the HTTP status the server returned and Message carries the reason the server gave rather than a generic string; StatusCode is null for a step that did not fail. SDK cmdlets surface transport failures as non-terminating errors, so call them with -ErrorAction Stop if you intend to catch them. Build request bodies with the SDK Initialize-VcfOps* cmdlets and forward only the parameters the caller actually bound: an optional field the caller did not supply must be absent from the JSON body rather than sent as an empty string, an empty array or null. ConfigValues is a hashtable and must be emitted as name/value pairs ordered by name with an ordinal case-sensitive sort. Do not use Invoke-RestMethod, Invoke-WebRequest, WebClient, HttpClient, curl, or another direct HTTP client. Keep the public command and manifest in place. The authoritative, spec-derived subset is docs/contract.json and its pinned provenance is docs/official_sources.json. The verifier uses a loopback VCF Operations service only; it never contacts a live VMware endpoint.
